answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying below it; draw 8 Zoo cards and keep 4, discarding 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards. Put all five Action cards side I up, with Animals in the leftmost slot (strength 1) and the other four randomly in the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, then 1, 2 and 3 by turn order.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C1 staggers Appeal 0/1/2/3; C3 places 1 worker active and 3 lying down; D takes 25 money; E draws 2 Final Scoring cards; F draws 8 and keeps 4; B puts Animals in the leftmost slot and all cards side I.

answers.answer: At setup, place 4 face-up Base Conservation Projects below the Association board in a 4-player game, and 3 in 2- or 3-player games. In a 2-player game, block the left level on the left base project, the middle level on the middle project, the right level on the right project, and the three spaces in the donation area's left column; neither player may use those spaces. There are no such blocks in 3- or 4-player games. Reveal the initial six-card display after everyone has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b: 4 face up in a 4-player game, otherwise 3; 5c: 2-player-only listed blocked spaces. Personal setup G reveals the 6 display cards after everyone chooses hand cards.

answers.answer: After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were in slots 1–3 one slot right, then put the used card in slot 1. Set strength before the action; each X-token spent then adds +1 strength, and X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action. You may spend any number, though strength above 5 sometimes adds no benefit, and may hold at most 5 X-tokens. An 'after finishing' effect resolves after the action is complete, including Action-card movement.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says shift all cards left of the empty slot right and place the used card in slot 1; X-tokens set strength before the action and gained tokens cannot boost it; maximum holding is 5; after-finishing effects occur after moving the cards.

answers.answer: You may not take a regular action that does nothing (including playing zero animals or building zero buildings). Instead, choose an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right. Slot strength and upgrade state do not matter. You cannot take this alternative if you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'You may not do nothing'; X-token action says select an Action card, move it to slot 1, shift intervening cards right, ignore strength/upgrade, and cannot use it at 5 X-tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional movement beyond that space and award the player who reached it 1 X-token. The break happens after that player's current turn ends, so they finish the turn. After the break, the token resets to the starting space and play continues clockwise with the next player; a normal break does not grant extra turns.
answers.evidence: Break track: on reaching the last space, the break takes place after the current turn, the player gets 1 X-token, extra steps are ignored, and the token resets after the break; Player Reference says play continues with the next player.

answers.answer: Both sides advance the Break token 2 spaces. On side I, either draw from the deck according to the strength table (up to 3 cards, with any required discard), or at strength 5+ snap exactly 1 display card of any reputation; snapping replaces deck draw. On side II, draw from the deck and/or the display within reputation range in any order using the upgraded table, or snap exactly 1 display card at strength 3+; snapping has no reputation restriction and is not combined with a deck draw. Refill display cards only after your turn is complete. There is no hand limit during a turn; discard to the limit only during breaks.
answers.evidence: Cards action: both sides advance Break 2; side I draw or snap at 5+, side II draw from deck and/or in-range display or snap at 3+; snapping ignores reputation; display replenishes at turn end; hand limit is checked at breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display folder matching your reputation and every lower-numbered folder. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action. At reputation 15, each further reputation step gives 1 appeal instead of moving the counter. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track: 'Within reputation range' is the matching folder plus lower-numbered folders; reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 further reputation gives 1 appeal per step; discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings, with total size no greater than strength and no duplicate building in that action. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. Your first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building along an edge. Build only on empty spaces and do not extend off-map, overlap, or cover water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Each kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately grants 1 appeal, once.
answers.evidence: Build side I/II limits and cost are stated under BUILD; placement rules specify first/later placement, water/rock and restricted spaces, kiosk spacing, and pavilion's one-time +1 appeal.

answers.answer: Build I allows standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo per zoo. Build II additionally allows the Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary; each is limited to one of its type per zoo. The supply contains four tiles of each special enclosure type. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table gives each type and side; supply has four of each special enclosure and each zoo one per type; unique buildings only come via Sponsor cards; fully covering all except water/rock grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used in later steps of that same action. Pay for each item before receiving that item's own benefits. Immediate placement or play effects resolve as encountered; 'after finishing' effects wait until the whole action is complete and the Action card has moved. When effects are simultaneous, the player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-token rules say earlier action bonuses may be used later and each item must be paid before its own benefits; Build II resolves placement bonuses before the next build and holds after-finishing bonuses; simultaneous effects are ordered by the owning player.

answers.answer: For each animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its cost, and house it before placing the card and resolving effects. A matching-continent partner zoo reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon on that animal, so a double icon gives a 6-money reduction. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the required size; put one animal in it and flip it to occupied. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may instead use the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if they fit, marking their indicated spaces with your supply tokens; special enclosures never flip. Required adjacent water/rock spaces apply, including to special-enclosure choices, and distinct adjacent terrain hexes are counted. Ordinary effects resolve immediately, including before a second animal; after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action is done and the card moves to slot 1. The player chooses the order of simultaneous effects.
answers.evidence: Animals action steps cover conditions, cost reduction per continent icon, empty standard enclosure and occupied flip, special-enclosure token marking, terrain adjacency, and immediate versus after-finishing effect timing.

answers.answer: Animals II permits animals from the display within your reputation range as well as from hand; pay an additional cost equal to the display folder number, and do not refill the display until your turn ends. At strength 5+, increase reputation by 1 at the very beginning of the action, so the larger range applies immediately. You may play animals with the upgrade-required condition.
answers.evidence: Animals side II: play from display within reputation range for folder-number cost; display is not replenished until turn ends; at strength 5+ reputation rises first; upgrade-required animal conditions are allowed.

answers.answer: Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, and only once per building, you may move all suitable animals that fit from standard enclosures, choosing separately for each. Mark the special-enclosure spaces required by each animal with tokens from your supply; never flip the special enclosure. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including water/rock adjacency, back to empty. If none meets all requirements, use the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size requirement, flip no standard enclosure.
answers.evidence: Build II permits moving all suitable animals that fit immediately and once per building; special spaces are marked with tokens. Special Rules gives the exact standard-enclosure selection and fallback sequence.

answers.answer: The four Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5. Side I performs exactly one task; side II may perform one or more different tasks whose total strength value is at most the action strength. You need an active worker for a task. If one of your workers is already on that task, place 2 workers to do it again; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot repeat it until after a break. Other players' workers do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association action lists strengths 2/3/4/5, side-I exactly one and worker repetition rules; side II permits different tasks within total strength.

answers.answer: Take partner zoos and universities from the available Association-board tiles and place them in the lowest empty spaces of their respective columns on your zoo map; take any printed space bonus immediately, and gain the university's reputation if it shows one. Board tiles are replenished after a break so each type is available exactly once, unless every player already has it. You cannot have partner zoos from duplicate continents, may have at most 4, and the third or fourth requires Association II; you cannot take a duplicate university. Universities are the only way to raise hand limit to 5; otherwise it is 3, checked at breaks.
answers.evidence: Association tasks describe board source, lowest available placement, immediate bonuses, partner continent/max and upgrade limits, no duplicate university, and university hand-limit benefit; break procedure replenishes tiles.

answers.answer: On Association I, conservation work can support a project already in play or play a project from hand and support it immediately; Association II can also play a new project from the display within reputation range for its folder-number cost. A new project goes in the leftmost space above the board, shifting existing cards right. To support, meet a condition without your token and put one token from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition; each player may support each project only once. Advance the conservation (and any shown reputation) reward, and take the uncovered-map bonus immediately, either before or after that project reward. If adding a project exceeds the player-count limit of 2, 3 or 4 cards above the board, discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to their owners' supplies, not their maps; previously activated map bonuses remain activated. Base projects below the board never move. The summary does not specify a separate overflow rule for a player's remaining left-edge tokens.
answers.evidence: Association conservation project work and support rules specify entry, conditions, once limit, token source and reward; over-limit cards and tokens return as described in the Association and Special Rules sections.

answers.answer: The animal's printed standard-enclosure size must match the release project's depicted size exactly, even if it can also live in a special enclosure. Before gaining conservation, lose only that animal's printed appeal, discard it and lose its icons. Keep its conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. If it could live in a special enclosure, first remove its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens if possible; otherwise flip an occupied standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting all requirements (including terrain), or, if none does, the smallest occupied one meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. The space freed is therefore special capacity first where possible, otherwise a standard enclosure according to that fallback.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild rules specify exact size match, losses and retained effects, then special-token removal and standard-enclosure selection/fallback.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand, with strength at least its level and conditions met; alternatively advance the Break token by strength and take that much money, even if fewer steps remain before the end. Sponsors II can play one or more cards from hand and/or display within reputation range, paying each display card's folder number; strength +1 must cover the total card levels. Resolve cards one at a time, completing each card's instant effects before the next, while holding after-finishing effects until the action ends. Display cards are replenished only at turn end. If using the side-II break/money option, take money twice the strength.
answers.evidence: Sponsors action spells out side-I single-card level rule and break option; side-II total level budget, hand/display source and cost, sequential resolution, end-of-turn refill and doubled break money.

answers.answer: Break order: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the relevant university); return Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, slide remaining cards down and refill; take income; reset the Break token. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not count, while empty special enclosures do. Income is appeal-track money, then kiosk income, then break-income effects on Sponsors and activated map bonuses. When display cards are taken during income, refill after each player; otherwise, when ordering effects, begin with the break initiator (or closest affected player) and proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Break procedure enumerates the sequence, hand limits, qualifying kiosk neighbors and income; it specifies per-player display refill and the clockwise ordering rule.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, take 5 money or a Bonus token at that space. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if no one reaches 10 before game end, everyone discards one before scoring. Check the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when your Appeal and Conservation counters are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained on another player's turn waits for your own turn or a break to trigger the end unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player finishes their turn and each other player takes one more turn; if triggered during a break, every player takes one more turn. Each Final Scoring card can award at most 4 conservation points. Victory Points equal your Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player with the most supported projects, then tied players share the win.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions specifies conservation rewards and 10-point discard, end timing and last turns, four-point Final Scoring cap, VP formula, and tiebreak.
